message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on 1/6 scale miniature replicas of synthesizers and samplers. These are non-functional scale models, 3D printed in PLA plastic, used as collectible decorations for dioramas.

The candidate headings are:
- 9503: toys, scale models. Subheading 9503.00.00 covers "reduced-size scale models and similar recreational models, working or not." The heading covers "tricycles, scooters, pedal cars; dolls; other toys; reduced-size ('scaled') models and similar recreational models, working or not; puzzles."
- 3926.40: statuettes and other ornamental articles of plastics. Its 3926.40.00 subheading is 3926.40.0000 in the HTSUS.
- 9505: festive articles. This does not fit.

The articles are for creating miniature studio dioramas. Models of dollhouse accessories are normally classified as toys in 9503. Collectible scale models for display are typically classified in 9503.00.00, specifically as "other" in 9503.00.00 with statistical suffixes. Because the articles are 1/6 scale accessories for dioramas (comparable to action-figure accessories), 9503 fits. The statistical suffix for "other toys" is 9503.00.0090 or similar. The HTSUS 9503.00.00 breakdown is: 9503.00.00 with suffixes 10 (Tricycles...), 21 (Dolls?), and 9503.00.0073 (Other toys), 9503.00.0080, 9503.00.0090. Recent revisions changed this into 9503.00.0073 for "Other" toys and 9503.00.0090 for "Other" items. For scale models, it would typically fall in the "Other" category.

Chapter 95 does not cover articles that are purely ornamental under Note 1, but collectible scale models are specifically named in heading 9503, so 9503 is appropriate.

I will choose 9503.00.0090.

{"hts_code": "9503.00.0090", "reason": "Non-functional 1/6-scale replicas of studio equipment for miniature dioramas are reduced-size scale models and similar recreational models of heading 9503, classified in the residual 'other' subheading."}
